captions.detailed: A perspective-control shift lens rendered in matte black. It features a large, tapered cylindrical main barrel containing the optical element, which tapers down to a narrower neck. At its base, a mechanical shift mechanism with a flat dovetail slider allows the entire optical block to shift laterally relative to the camera mount interface. A rotational collar at the base permits the shift axis to rotate 360 degrees.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a perspective-control shift camera lens using CadQuery. The model should feature a tapered cylindrical outer barrel, an inner optical block with a glass lens, a rotating collar at the base, and a prismatic shift slider mechanism that allows lateral adjustment perpendicular to the optical axis.
captions.factory: The design starts with a base mount plate and a revolute rotation ring modeled as concentric cylinders. The shift mechanism is constructed using rectangular boxes to form a dovetail guide and slider block. The main lens barrel is built by lofting or unioning multiple coaxial cylinders and cones of varying diameters to form the tapered outer profile, which is then hollowed out. A thin glass disc cylinder is placed inside the front opening of the barrel to represent the optical element. The parts are structured into an articulated assembly with a continuous joint for the rotation ring and a prismatic joint for the lateral shifting block.
